record.original_question: For functions defined on a finite interval, what is the full characterization of one-parameter families of fractional integral operators I^alpha and associated fractional derivative operators D^alpha that satisfy the six desiderata HL1-HL6: linearity of I^alpha and D^alpha, the semigroup law I^alpha1 o I^alpha2 = I^(alpha1+alpha2), the left-inverse identity D^alpha o I^alpha = Id, existence of the limits D^alpha -> D^0 as alpha -> 0 and D^alpha -> D^1 as alpha -> 1, D^0 equal to the identity, and D^1 equal to the first derivative?

evidence.quote: The families of the operators I^alpha, alpha >= 0 and D^alpha, alpha >= 0 can be interpreted as fractional integrals and fractional derivatives, respectively, if they satisfy the following six properties (called desiderata in [30]).

Deduce a characterization of the fractional integrals for the functions defined on a finite interval that satisfy the desiderata presented in the previous subsection (the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals are one of such families that satisfies essentially stronger conditions compared to those from desiderata, see Theorem 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider functions defined on a finite real interval $[a,b]$. Determine and fully characterize all one-parameter families of linear operators $\{I^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ (to be interpreted as fractional integrals) and the associated one-parameter families of linear operators $\{D^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ (to be interpreted as fractional derivatives) acting on suitable spaces of functions on $[a,b]$ that simultaneously satisfy the following six desiderata:

(HL1) For every $\alpha\ge 0$, $I^{\alpha}$ is linear.

(HL2) For every $\alpha\ge 0$, $D^{\alpha}$ is linear.

(HL3) Index (semigroup) law: $I^{\alpha_1}\circ I^{\alpha_2}=I^{\alpha_1+\alpha_2}$ for all $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\ge 0$.

(HL4) Left-inverse property: $D^{\alpha}\circ I^{\alpha}=\mathrm{Id}$ for all $\alpha\ge 0$.

(HL5) The limits $\lim_{\alpha\to 0^{+}} D^{\alpha}=D^{0}$ and $\lim_{\alpha\to 1^{-}} D^{\alpha}=D^{1}$ exist (in an appropriate operator topology on the chosen function space).

(HL6) $D^{0}=\mathrm{Id}$ and $D^{1}=\dfrac{d}{dx}$.

Provide a complete description of every such pair of families $(I^{\alpha},D^{\alpha})$ on a finite interval, going beyond the Riemann–Liouville family (which is known to satisfy these desiderata together with stronger additional conditions).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be posed as an open problem in the line of work by Luchko on general fractional integrals and derivatives. While Luchko's 2023 paper "The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval" extends Sonin-kernel-based GFI/GFD to finite intervals and provides families satisfying versions of the desiderata, a full characterization of all one-parameter families on a finite interval satisfying exactly the six Hardy–Littlewood/Hilfer–Luchko desiderata (without strengthening them) does not appear to have been completed; on the half-line a uniqueness-type characterization is known under stronger conditions, and the finite-interval case is presented as an extension/open question.

status_evidence.title: The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces general fractional integrals and derivatives on a finite interval, extending Sonin-kernel theory previously developed on the positive semi-axis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends GFI/GFD to finite intervals but a complete characterization under exactly the six desiderata is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Fractional derivatives and the fundamental theorem of fractional calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Under some reasonable conditions there exists precisely one unique family of fractional integrals (Riemann–Liouville) on the half-line, with derivatives defined as their left inverses.
status_evidence.claim: A uniqueness/characterization theorem is available on the half-line under stronger conditions; the finite-interval analogue is presented as a further question.
